To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antibiotic-resistant bacteria show widespread sensitivity to antimicrobial peptide, and this sensitivity is due to changes in bacterial lipopolysaccheride regulation.
multidrug-resistant E. coli show a high frequency collateral sensitivity to antimicrobials, which may arise through regulatory changes shaping lipopolysacchride composition of the bacterial surface.

antibiotic-resistant bacteria have a high frequency (up to 70% of strains) of collateral sensitivity to a broad panel of antimicrobial peptides, and that this collateral sensitivity may be exploited to enhance the activity of antibiotics against antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antimicrobial agents and the discovery of new antibiotic resistance mechanisms.
the identification of antimicrobials and antimicrobial combinations that are effective against multidrug-resistant E. coli.
understanding the mechanisms of collateral sensitivity to peptides in antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains and how to exploit this knowledge for developing new therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resistance to antibiotics can lead to collateral sensitivity to antimicrobials peptides.

antimicrobial peptides are promising alternatives to antibiotics, especially in the case of multidrug-resistant bacteria, and that their combination with antibiotics may enhance the activity of antibiotics and slow down the evolution of resistance.

antibiotic resistance is not necessarily accompanied by resistance to antimicrobial peptides and, therefore, antimicrobial peptides can be used as adjuvants to enhance the efficacy of antibiotics against antibiotic resistant bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antibiotic-resistant bacteria are sensitive to antimicrobial peptides and, in particular, to the antimicrobial peptide GLA.
antibiotic-resistant bacteria are more susceptible to antimicrobial peptides than their antibiotic-susceptible ancestors.
antimicrobial peptides are promising adjuvants for antibiotic therapy of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotic-resistant bacteria show collateral sensitivity to antimicrobials peptides.
antimicrobial peptides are a valuable tool to combat multidrug-resistant infections.
antimicrobial peptides can be used as adjuvants to enhance the efficacy of antibiotics in the treatment of multidrug-resistant infections.
